what_its_for: Reslizumab is used as an add-on treatment for adults with severe asthma that is related to high levels of a type of white blood cell called eosinophils. It helps reduce the number of asthma attacks (flare-ups) and makes it easier to breathe. It does NOT work as a rescue inhaler and should not be used for sudden asthma attacks.
how_to_take: Reslizumab is given as an intravenous (IV) infusion directly into your vein by a healthcare professional in a clinic or hospital setting. You cannot take this medicine at home on your own. Each infusion takes about 20 to 50 minutes. You will be monitored by your healthcare team during and after each infusion for signs of a serious allergic reaction.
dosing: The usual dose is 3 mg per kilogram of your body weight, given once every 4 weeks (once a month). Your doctor will calculate the exact dose based on your weight. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never try to adjust your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss or skip your scheduled infusion appointment, contact your doctor or clinic as soon as possible to reschedule. Try to keep all your appointments so the medicine can work properly. Do not try to double up on doses.
storage: Reslizumab is stored and prepared by healthcare professionals at the clinic. You do not need to store this medication at home. At the clinic, it is kept refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C) and protected from light. It should never be frozen.
what_to_avoid: Do not use reslizumab as a quick-relief or rescue inhaler during a sudden asthma attack — always keep your rescue inhaler with you. Do not stop taking your other asthma medicines (such as inhaled corticosteroids) unless your doctor tells you to. Avoid missing your scheduled infusion appointments. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, or supplements you are taking before starting treatment.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency help RIGHT AWAY if you experience: sudden or severe chest tightness, shortness of breath, or wheezing; swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat; dizziness, feeling faint, or a rapid heartbeat; hives, rash, or severe itching; these could be signs of a serious allergic reaction called anaphylaxis, which can happen during or after your infusion. Also contact your doctor if your asthma symptoms get worse or if you notice any new or unusual symptoms.
when_it_works: Reslizumab may start to reduce asthma attacks within a few weeks, but it can take several months to feel the full benefit. It is important to keep all your infusion appointments even if you feel well. Do not stop treatment without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Reslizumab is only approved for adults 18 years of age and older. It has not been studied enough in children to know if it is safe or effective for them. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, talk to your doctor before starting this medicine, as the effects on unborn babies and nursing infants are not fully known. Older adults can use reslizumab, but your doctor will monitor you closely.
